THE LOCAL MEANING

What it is.

A Cape Hatteras and Outer Banks red-drum trip associated with a seasonal run. “Old drum” and “big drum” refer to large red drum. This page covers the red-drum meaning; black-drum runs in Texas or Delaware Bay are different trip traditions.

How it is fished.

Surf bait fishing or inlet boat fishing.

The research describes surf bait fishing and inlet boat options. The existing Cape Hatteras profile is the beach-access match. Choose the shore route or a named boat departure before you compare equipment. Fall is the main cited run, with a spring run also noted; neither guarantees fish on a chosen day.

Planning format: Half day or full day; surf or inlet. Confirm the actual duration with the provider.

Before you go.

Is every “drum run” the same fishery?

No. This page means red drum around Cape Hatteras and the Outer Banks. Other regions use drum run for black drum. Name the species and water when you ask for a trip.

What seasonal window does the evidence support?

Fall is the main cited run. A spring run also occurs. A seasonal account does not confirm current availability. Use the linked authority for current rules.

What must I confirm before I book this trip?

Confirm whether the service is shore instruction, transport, or a boat trip. Ask about bait, rods, sand spikes, and fish-release equipment. Check the beach-access plan, any vehicle permit, and a weather alternative. Castward has no confirmed guide inventory for this trip type.
